items.title: Burkina/Lutte contre la fraude : La CNLF saisit des produits d’une valeur de plus de 141 millions en deux semaines
items.description: Burkina/Lutte contre la fraude : La CNLF saisit des produits d’une valeur de plus de 141 millions en deux semaines Ouagadougou, 5 août 2026 (AIB) – La Coordination nationale de lutte contre la fraude (CNLF) a annoncé, mercredi à Ouagadougou, avoir saisi des produits frauduleux d’une valeur cumulée de 141 383 500 FCFA lors d’opérations menées entre le 20 juillet et le 5 août 2026 contre le détournement de carburant subventionné, la contrebande et le commerce de produits prohibés. Selon le coordonnateur, les opérations ont notamment permis la saisie, le 20 juillet sur la voie de contournement de Ouagadougou, d’un camion-citerne transportant 10 000 litres de gasoil subventionné destinés illicitement à une usine de fabrication de fer et de tôles. La cargaison est évaluée à 11,9 millions FCFA, avec un manque à gagner estimé à 5,37 millions FCFA pour l’État. Le 25 juillet, à Karpala, les agents ont également intercepté 136 cartons et 153 paquets de boissons énergisantes alcoolisées de marque Ice, ainsi que 25 cartons de chicha, en violation de l’arrêté interministériel du 24 juin 2024 interdisant ces produits au Burkina Faso. Le lendemain, à Poè, dans la province de la Sissili, la CNLF a saisi 160 colis de sachets plastiques interdits transportés par deux tricycles, pour une valeur de 4,45 millions FCFA, conformément à la loi de décembre 2024 sur les emballages plastiques. À Kouba, le 29 juillet, trois polytanks de 1 000 litres de gasoil subventionné ont été interceptés alors qu’ils ravitaillaient illicitement une entreprise, causant un préjudice de 1,611 million FCFA au Trésor public. Le coordonnateur a également annoncé qu’une importante saisie de consommables médicaux importés en contrebande a été effectuée le 3 août à Ouagadougou. Elle comprend notamment des fils médicaux, des kits médicaux, des seringues, des pommades à la pénicilline ainsi que 76 cartons d’anabolisants, pour une valeur globale estimée à 68,017 millions FCFA. Le 4 août, les équipes de la CNLF ont intercepté à Koubri un camion en situation de récidive déchargeant 13 000 litres de gasoil subventionné destinés à une société de granite, occasionnant un manque à gagner de 6,981 millions FCFA pour le Trésor public. Le même jour, à l’issue d’une enquête de plus de deux mois dans la zone de Zabré, un camion-remorque transportant en contrebande du sucre, de l’huile alimentaire, du riz, de la farine, des boissons alcoolisées, des tomates, des cubes alimentaires et des spaghettis a été saisi. La marchandise est estimée à 34,447 millions FCFA, en infraction avec le Code des douanes. Pour Dr Mohamadi Compaoré, ces interventions visaient à protéger les consommateurs, préserver les recettes publiques et défendre l’économie nationale contre les pratiques frauduleuses. « La fraude compromet les ressources de l’État, le financement du développement et la protection des consommateurs », a affirmé Dr Compaoré. Il a rappelé que le carburant subventionné est destiné exclusivement aux ménages et ne peut légalement bénéficier aux entreprises industrielles. Le coordonnateur national a enfin salué « le dévouement » des agents de la CNLF et remercié les populations pour leur collaboration, les invitant à poursuivre leur vigilance afin de renforcer la lutte contre la fraude sous toutes ses formes. Agence d’information du Burkina GIP/VAT/yos

items.title: Abdul El-Sayed’s Next Big Challenge
items.description: T he Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed made the customary call for unity after a hard-fought primary against a fellow Democrat. “Always magnanimity in victory,” he told a packed crowd of supporters, adding that “however much we might disagree with our Democratic opponent, there is so much more that unites us than divides us.” But just minutes earlier, one of his most famous endorsers was pushing a much different message. “Everyone being like, Abdul has a fuck-ton of work to do mending bridges , here’s the fucking take-nuke for you, okay? You are all unbelievably Islamophobic pieces of shit,” Hasan Piker, the provocative left-wing Twitch streamer El-Sayed has embraced on the campaign trail, told some of his millions of followers. Piker went on to challenge would-be holdouts in the party to back El-Sayed: “Do you want to fucking win or not?” Democrats in Michigan do, in fact, want to win in November, but they find themselves in a predicament over how to get everyone on board. El-Sayed, a progressive, eked out a victory over the more moderate Haley Stevens in a historically expensive and high-profile showdown between the party’s insurgent and centrist wings. The closeness of the race—El-Sayed led by about one point when the AP declared him the victor this morning—surprised many people, given that a number of polls showed the 41-year-old doctor with a double-digit lead over the four-term congresswoman. The narrow margin of victory has, predictably, sparked a blizzard of thoughts about what lessons Democrats should garner from El-Sayed’s victory as the party barrels toward November. The candidate has suggested that he doesn’t plan to moderate his platform; he ended a news conference this morning by giving a version of his campaign slogan, asking Michiganders to join a “movement to get money out of politics, so we can put money back in pockets and finally guarantee the promise of health care through Medicare for all.” At the same time, he insisted that Democratic harmony would be crucial in the face of what he predicted would be an onslaught of negative attacks from his Republican opponents. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, the chair of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, were happy to comply. They endorsed El-Sayed’s candidacy this morning, praising his “energetic campaign.” (Both had originally endorsed Stevens.) Michigan State Senator Mallory McMorrow, who ended her bid for the Democratic nomination last month, announced her support for El-Sayed last night before the race had even been called. Stevens also added her endorsement this morning. But much of the common ground ended there. The takes on what El-Sayed should do and the lessons the party should learn from his victory are so abundant in part because the stakes are so high. Democrats will struggle to recapture the Senate if they do not win the race in Michigan. Adam Green, a co-founder of the Progressive Change Campaign Committee, told us that El-Sayed’s win “sends a signal to every other Democratic politician in America that you can cross very powerful interests and still win if the people are on your side.” Green suggested that El-Sayed doesn’t need to perform some grand pivot to appeal to general-election voters who may be skeptical about his leftist views: “We believe that Abdul El-Sayed and candidates like him are more electable in a general election because we’re living in an outsider moment and people in all political parties and independents want someone who will shake up a broken system, not be a creature of it.” Asked about Green’s comment, another Democratic strategist, who requested anonymity to be frank, was, well, frank. “What the fuck is he talking about? Now you’re pushing an ideological agenda and not trying to win,” the strategist told us, before addressing El-Sayed himself. “You clearly need to pivot,” this person said. “A lot of the people in the party don’t like you!” The returns highlighted clear vulnerabilities for the new nominee. El-Sayed performed well in highly educated, mostly white and affluent communities, including some of Michigan’s college towns, while trailing Stevens in some working-class areas and Black neighborhoods. Adam Jentleson, a former Democratic Senate leadership aide, posted on X that El-Sayed begins the general election as an underdog. He predicted that the Democrat would underperform his polls “because a lot of normie Dems are voting against him,” and added that El-Sayed should try to win over these folks by being “a little less rigidly left-wing, and a little more heterodox.” El-Sayed said today that the primary would “pale in comparison to the cynicism” that would come from his Republican opponent, former Representative Mike Rogers, and President Trump during the general election. That prediction seemed to come true just hours later, as the National Republican Senatorial Committee released its first ad of the general election. “Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed—the most radical Senate candidate in America,” the ad’s narrator begins, casting away any sense of subtlety before going on to link the Democrat to the Muslim Brotherhood and describe him as “too dangerous” for Michigan. (The ad uses the full name of the candidate attempting to become the nation’s first Muslim American senator at a time when some Republicans have been fomenting Islamophobia.) [ Read: The Republican who wants to banish his own constituents ] Michigan continues to swing between Republicans and Democrats—Trump won the state in 2016 and 2024. The president wasted no time weighing in on El-Sayed’s victory this morning, calling him a “Communist loser who hates Jews and Israel.” El-Sayed ran as an unabashed critic of Israel and AIPAC, which spent tens of millions of dollars backing Stevens. Trump predicted that, with El-Sayed, the “Dumocrats crazy policies will only get worse” and called his win “great news for the Republican Party.” Lis Smith, a Democratic operative who advised McMorrow in the primary, told us that El-Sayed should focus on broadening his coalition, adding that she feels that “he has not tried to do that one iota during this primary.” Rogers, who ran unopposed, came just about 20,000 votes shy of winning a Senate seat in 2024. El-Sayed bashed Rogers last night and this morning, aiming to cast him as an avatar of the corporate elite that has raised prices and left everyday Michiganders struggling. He also tied Rogers closely to Trump, who polls show is unpopular in the state. [ Read: America’s most divided state loves its extremes ] The call for Democratic unity is a new one for El-Sayed. He showed no hesitation about blasting the party as he pursued its nomination, telling a group of young voters last month that “the Democratic Party brand right now is so bullshit.” El-Sayed also used his primary victory to attack politics as usual—clearly implying that Democrats have been engaged in it for far too long. Although El-Sayed’s victory was the main event this week, several other races across the country complicated the idea that the Democratic Party has been seized by the progressive movement. In Missouri, former Representative Cori Bush lost handily to Representative Wesley Bell, the moderate who originally ousted her from her seat two years ago. In Washington State, centrist incumbent Marie Gluesenkamp Perez beat back a challenge from the left to win a primary for a district that Trump carried in 2024. Moderate Democrats in Virginia prevailed in two key congressional primaries, while left-leaning candidates claimed victories in two congressional primaries in Michigan. The murkiness of the results shows that the party is stuck in a state of tension. Joel Payne, a Democratic strategist whose organization, MoveOn, endorsed El-Sayed, told us that although the process appears chaotic, it is necessary for a party trying to redefine itself and recover from traumatic losses in 2024. “Democrats tried an era where we swept things under the rug and we tried to sort things out before it got in front of voters,” he said. “That doesn’t work. We’re in a different era.” Instead, he advised, the party needs to openly “have the fights, let it get messy, and then put it back together on the back side.” Things in Michigan are certainly messy. Now El-Sayed and his fellow Democrats need to put them back together over the next 13 weeks if Democrats hope to win back the Senate in November.

items.title: Ouahigouya : pour avoir violé une mineure de 16 ans, il écope d’une peine d’emprisonnement de 07 ans
items.description: Ouahigouya : pour avoir violé une mineure de 16 ans, il écope d'une peine d’emprisonnement de 07 ans Ouahigouya, 5 août 2026 (AIB)-Le tribunal de grande instance de Ouahigouya a délibéré au terme de l'audience correctionnelle du mercredi 22 juillet sur le dossier de S.I, poursuivi pour viol sur mineure de 16 ans. Le prévenu, reconnu coupable, écope d'une peine d’emprisonnement de sept (07) ans dont trois (03) ans ferme, assortie d'une amende. Les faits se sont déroulés dans la soirée du 05 juin 2026 au secteur 10 de la cité de Naaba Kango. La victime S.C, âgée de 16 ans au moment des faits, est née le 29 octobre 2009 et vit sous le toit parental. À la barre, le prévenu S.I, jeune orpailleur âgé de 19 ans, a reconnu avoir eu un rapport sexuel avec le consentement de S.C, qu'il affirme connaître depuis un certain temps dans le quartier. « Je l'ai croisée dans la rue et comme je l'avais invitée plusieurs fois sans succès, ce jour elle a accepté de venir avec moi. Une fois chez moi, nous avons eu un rapport sexuel et elle est repartie », a précisé le prévenu qui soutiendra par la suite devant le juge qu'il ignorait l'âge de la victime. À la question de savoir s'il connaît la victime, S.I répondra par l'affirmative, et par rapport à l'âge de la victime, le prévenu dira qu'il estime son âge à 16 ans. Le tribunal a posé la question de savoir quelle serait sa réaction si c'était son propre enfant mineure qu'un homme abusait. S.I a répondu sans ambages : « Si ma fille est consentante, c'est normal, je n'en voudrais pas à celui qui a commis l'acte. » La victime S.C, qui a donné son accord pour que les débats soient publics et non à huis clos, a livré sa version des faits au tribunal. « Mon père m'a envoyé faire des emplettes et j'ai croisé S.I dans la rue ; il m'a invitée à venir chez lui, juste à côté, et j'ai refusé. Avec la complicité d'un ami, S.I m'a contrainte avec un couteau à rejoindre une maisonnette et, quand je me suis retrouvée à l'intérieur, son ami a condamné la porte de l'extérieur ; c'est ainsi qu'il m'a déshabillée de force avant de passer à l'acte. », a soutenu S.C. Le prévenu a reconnu qu'il portait sur lui un couteau, qu'il a retiré et déposé sur la table, mais a nié l'avoir utilisé pour menacer la victime. À la question du tribunal de savoir si S.C a crié au secours, elle a répondu oui, tout en précisant qu'il n'y avait personne à côté. Le parquet a voulu savoir si S.C avait déjà entretenu des relations sexuelles auparavant, la victime a été catégorique : « Je ne connaissais pas d'homme avant l'acte avec S.I. » Intervenant pour clarifier la situation, le procureur a annoncé, à la grande stupéfaction du géniteur de S.C, présent à l'audience, qu'au vu de l'expertise médicale demandée par le parquet au cours de l'instruction, il ressort que S.C serait déjà sexuellement active au moment des faits. Dans son réquisitoire, le procureur a estimé qu'au regard de la loi, il s'agit d'un acte grave que S.I a posé, eu égard à l'âge de la victime dont l'acte de naissance confirme qu'elle est née le 29 octobre 2009 (16 ans), donc mineure au moment des faits. « Conformément à l'article 533 du code pénal, les enfants sont protégés ; l'article précise qu'étant mineure, en cas de relation sexuelle même avec consentement, la loi est formelle et considère que c'est un viol », a laissé entendre le représentant du ministère public. En répression, le ministère public a requis une peine de prison de 36 mois dont 06 mois ferme et une amende de 100 000 FCFA. Le procureur a soutenu sa décision en tenant compte de l'âge de la victime et du prévenu (16 ans et 19 ans), tout en estimant que S.I est un délinquant primaire sans antécédent judiciaire. Au délibéré en date du 29 juillet 2026, le tribunal correctionnel, statuant contradictoirement et en premier ressort, a déclaré S.I coupable des faits qui lui sont reprochés. En répression, le tribunal a condamné S.I à sept (07) ans de prison dont trois (03) ans ferme et 600 000 FCFA d'amende dont 100 000 FCFA ferme. Le tribunal a donné acte au représentant de la victime, qui a déclaré ne pas se constituer partie civile. Comme le prévoit la loi, S.I a 10 jours pour faire appel du jugement. Agence d'information du Burkina PN/LG/ATA

items.title: Mercato : c’est officiel, Dion Lopy quitte l’Espagne pour rejoindre l’Arabie Saoudite
items.description: Dion Lopy change de continent. Le milieu de terrain sénégalais, qui évoluait à Almería depuis trois ans, s'est engagé avec le club saoudien d'Al-Ittihad, où il retrouvera une importante communauté sénégalaise installée sur place. Ce transfert surprend, car le joueur de 24 ans venait tout juste de prolonger son bail avec le club andalou jusqu'en 2030. Plusieurs écuries européennes, dont Aston Villa, s'étaient d'ailleurs positionnées pour le recruter. Finalement, Lopy n'aura pas eu l'occasion de disputer une saison supplémentaire sur le Vieux Continent : il file directement vers l'Arabie saoudite, où il a paraphé un contrat courant jusqu'en 2029 avec l'un des clubs les plus décorés du football arabe. De son côté, la direction d'Almería a confirmé le départ de son ancien milieu de terrain, saluant les 105 apparitions effectuées sous ses couleurs et remerciant le joueur pour son engagement durant ces trois saisons. Le club a précisé que Lopy avait déjà quitté le stage de préparation de Marbella pour rallier sa nouvelle destination. L'opération rapporterait environ 13 millions d'euros aux Andalous, auxquels pourraient s'ajouter 6 millions supplémentaires sous forme de bonus. Sur les réseaux sociaux, Al-Ittihad a officialisé la nouvelle avec un message de bienvenue au joueur, tandis qu'Almería lui a rendu hommage pour sa contribution au club durant son passage en Liga. items.title: Real Madrid make Vinicius Jr improved contract offer
items.description: Real Madrid have made Vinicius Jr an improved contract offer as they look to keep the Brazil winger at the Bernabeu. The 26-year-old has entered the final 12 months of his contract and has attracted interest from Arsenal in recent weeks. Talks over a new deal at Real were at an impasse, but the Spanish side have now made a new offer to Vinicius, who is understood to be appreciative of the fresh terms. Real now await Vinicius’ decision, but senior managers – including returning head coach Jose Mourinho – are now hopeful he will renew. It is understood Real are expecting a response within hours rather than days. If Vinicius rejects the contract, Arsenal are willing to accelerate their interest in the Brazilian. Vinicius signed a contract extension at Real three years ago which runs until 2027, and the club and his representatives have been in talks over a fresh deal for the past 18 months. He returned to the club on Monday for his first pre-season training session and medical assessment following his World Cup campaign with Brazil. Vinicius, who has made 375 appearances for Real in all competitions, scoring 128 goals, is believed to want recognition as Los Blancos’ top star financially. However, Real are traditionally strict about maintaining their salary structure under president Florentino Perez. Vinicius has publicly described Real as “the club of my dreams” and said he hopes to remain there “for many years”. Arsenal have identified the Brazilian as their priority left-wing target should his position change.

items.title: Mike Johnson Would Prefer Not To
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. This morning, House Speaker Mike Johnson finally broke his silence on the scandal engulfing Representative Max Miller of Ohio. Well, sort of—Johnson didn’t have much to say. “I haven’t spoken to Max about this in the last few days. Of course, I will,” he told Politico . Johnson said that Miller, a fellow Republican, was taking the allegations seriously (despite evidence to the contrary ) and that a House Ethics Committee process should “play out.” (Miller requested the investigation this week, an apparent stalling tactic.) Johnson added, “There’s all sorts of domestic events going on with 435 members of Congress all the time. It’s not my business to get engaged in it.” This raises the question of what Johnson does think the speaker’s business is. One might imagine that the Miller situation would concern Johnson for several reasons. Johnson positions himself as a staunch social conservative and defender of morality; Miller has been accused of domestic abuse against his ex-wife and toddler daughter, and of illegal drug use. (Miller has denied the abuse allegations and said that although he has used illegal drugs in the past, he no longer does.) For his caucus, it’s a big distraction from any midterm messaging that the Republican Party might wish to do in the last 100 days before elections. The scandal also puts another GOP seat in play in November ; Miller said on CNN last night that Donald Trump had told him that it would be a “tough” race to win. If Miller drops out by Monday afternoon, Republicans in Ohio can replace him on the ballot, but it’s not clear how quickly the Ethics Committee process will move. If Johnson doesn’t think that his job includes protecting the moral reputation of the House, his small and endangered House majority, or the prospects of the Republican Party more broadly, he must have some other idea about his role. What that might be is mysterious. Passing legislation would seem like an obvious answer, but the 119th Congress has been one of the least productive in history. Legislators have succeeded in enacting just 104 laws since January 2025. That’s the lowest number by far since at least 1947 —only the 274 laws passed last Congress even come close. This is especially remarkable because Republicans hold control over both chambers. Legislative leaders have also yielded some of their power over budgets, one of their most basic duties, to the White House. Even worse, 2025 saw the longest complete shutdown of the federal government in history, as legislators failed to fund the government for 43 days. Some of the blame for this unproductivity belongs to the Senate, where the GOP edge is narrow and where rules mean that a Democratic minority can more easily block legislation. But senators are at least filling their time with other official duties, such as confirming presidential appointments, that the House doesn’t have. Another basic congressional duty is oversight of the executive branch, but the House has done little to investigate or shed light on what the administration is doing, much less hold it to account. In May, Johnson called a recess rather than hold a vote condemning Trump’s war in Iran, after it became clear that the nonbinding measure would pass. (The House has since passed a similar resolution.) Johnson isn’t setting some sort of broader agenda for the legislature either. That, too, has been left to Trump, who seems to have been interested in only two bills: the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, passed last year, and the SAVE America Act, currently and perhaps permanently bottled up in the Senate. Johnson’s deference to Trump has reportedly led the president to joke in private that he has “two jobs: being president and being speaker.” That’s rather demeaning for Johnson, but given how Trump dominates the House, one might expect that Johnson would pay close attention to what the president says and does. Yet Johnson has a consistent pattern of pleading ignorance when asked about controversial statements or actions by Trump or his administration. In a characteristic example, Johnson dodged a question in October about cuts to funding for special education: “I’ve been so busy on this; I’ve not had a chance to dig into the details.” Busy on what , precisely? In fairness to Johnson, he’s working in a difficult environment with just a seven-seat majority, a rebellious right flank, and a mercurial president. But he does have some power when he wants to use it—as became apparent this week. On Monday, the House Ethics Committee found that Representative Chuck Edwards of North Carolina, a Republican, had “engaged in persistent unprofessional and inappropriate conduct towards two young female staffers” and had likely “violated House rules related to sexual harassment and hostile workplaces.” (Edwards denied that any of his conduct had been intended as a sexual or romantic advance.) Yesterday, CNN reported that House leaders were pressuring Edwards to drop his reelection bid. Early this morning, Edwards did just that. By attempting to remain distant from the Miller scandal, Johnson is allowing Miller to claim, as he did in an interview last night, that “Speaker Mike Johnson, everyone else—they’re standing behind me.” Johnson’s reluctance to become involved in a messy, lurid story like this one is understandable, but it’s also one of the burdens that falls on leaders. By declining to bear it, Johnson may help ensure that he doesn’t have to worry about the duties of the speaker when the new Congress opens next January. Related: A family tragedy in the age of Trump Mike Johnson is tuning out the news cycle to focus on self-care, Alexandra Petri writes. ( From 2025 ) Here are three new stories from The Atlantic : The once-shameless president is deeply embarrassed. Liberals are now fighting a two-front war. Anne Applebaum: Putin’s human safari is the dystopian future of war. Today’s News Abdul El-Sayed defeated Representative Haley Stevens in Michigan’s Democratic U.S. Senate primary, marking a significant win for the party’s progressive wing after a tight race. He will face Republican Mike Rogers in November in a battleground contest that could help determine control of the Senate. The cyclosporiasis outbreak has reached six more states , bringing the total to 15 states. The CDC said there are more than 22,000 confirmed or suspected cases, 517 hospitalizations, and two deaths linked to the outbreak. The White House has declassified FBI records showing that the bureau opened a 2017 investigation into whether President Trump had been acting on Russia’s behalf when he fired then–FBI Director James Comey, according to administration officials. They said that the inquiry had ultimately found no evidence to support the theory. Evening Read Illustration by Mark Harris* What Happened to al-Qaeda? By Graeme Wood Since September 11, 2001, al‑Qaeda has pulled off exactly one fatal attack inside the United States. If you remember the details of that attack, you probably spend too much time thinking about terrorism. On December 6, 2019, in Pensacola, Florida, a 21-year-old Royal Saudi Air Force officer took out a legally acquired Glock pistol and killed three U.S. sailors at a naval air base, before police arrived and killed him. The shooter, an affiliate of al‑Qaeda’s branch in Yemen, had been on the base for flight training. I was in Taif, Saudi Arabia, at the time, and the Saudis I met said they were sorry about the incident but relieved that after 18 years of terrorist R&D, the most ferocious blow al‑Qaeda could strike on the path of jihad was not much worse than the kind of mundane workplace violence that we Americans regularly inflict on ourselves. items.title: Arms proliferation: NSCDC dismisses 2, exonerates mining commander
items.description: By Omega Ajayi The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC on Wednesday said it has dismissed two operatives of its Mining Marshal squad for unlawfully providing illegal miners with firearms. Commandant General of the Corps, Prof. Ahmed Audi, said that the actions of the two personnel contradicted established guidelines. The corps however exonerated the Mining Marshals Commander, ACC John Onoja, whose team was allegedly linked to the diversion of N2 billion and cover up of circumstances leading to the death of a personnel, Levi Agada in Nasarawa state. Speaking through Corps National Public Relations Officer, Babawale Afolabi, the NSCDC boss said the actions of the dismissed personnel constituted grave misconduct, professional negligence and conduct prejudicial to the discipline and operational integrity of the corps. “Consequently, both personnel have been dismissed from the service and recommended for prosecution in accordance with the law,” he said. According to him, the dismissal of the officers was based on the recommendation for prosecution of the personnel following the operational incident of February 18, 2026 in Nasarawa, which led to the death of their location commander, Levi Agada. The NSCDC boss said comprehensive investigations had cleared Onoja, the lead prosecutor and other management team members of alleged complicity. “Allegations suggesting otherwise were found to be false and without factual basis,” he said. According to Audi, investigations also established that there was no evidence of premeditated intent against the deceased. items.title: Measures to tackle security challenges in Southeast Nigeria
items.description: By Ike Nwachukwu I am deeply honoured to participate in this important summit. Permit me to commend the Government and the organisers for convening this timely dialogue. At a time when our nation continues to confront complex security challenges, there can be no substitute for honest reflection, strategic thinking, and genuine collaboration. After many decades in military service, diplomacy, and public life, I have come to appreciate one enduring truth: Security is not simply the absence of violence. It is the presence of justice, trust, opportunity, and legitimate authority. When these pillars weaken, insecurity begins long before the first gunshot is fired. Today, the South-East faces significant security challenges. These are often described in terms of kidnappings, violent crimes, attacks on public institutions, and threats to law and order. Yet these manifestations are, in many respects, symptoms rather than the underlying disease. The deeper challenge is the gradual erosion of confidence-confidence in institutions, in leadership, in one another, and sometimes even in the future itself. No security architecture can succeed where trust has collapsed. Military force is indispensable. But military force alone has never permanently solved a political, economic, or social problem. Armies create the space for peace. Societies must then build the peace. That distinction is fundamental. Allow me, therefore, to offer six reflections. First, security begins with intelligence-not firepower. The most successful operations are those that prevent violence before it occurs. That requires intelligence that is timely, accurate, and locally generated. Communities must see security agencies as trusted partners rather than distant institutions to be feared. The greatest intelligence asset any nation possesses is not technology. It is that citizen who believes that the government will protect rather than punish. Trust remains the most effective force multiplier. Second, every community must become a stakeholder in security. Security cannot remain the exclusive responsibility of the Armed Forces, the Police, or other security agencies. Parents. Teachers. Traditional rulers. Religious leaders. Youth organisations. Professional associations. Market unions. Town unions. Every one of them possesses influence, local knowledge, and moral authority that no government institution can replicate. Security succeeds when citizens become participants rather than spectators. Third, development is one of the strongest forms of security. Young people who possess hope are less vulnerable to being recruited by less patriotic Nigerians who find them easy tools because of their frustration. These young men and women therefore are used to perpetrate heinous crimes against society. Roads. Schools. Healthcare. Digital infrastructure. Agriculture. Industrial investment. Employment opportunities. These are not merely development projects. They are strategic investments in national security. Every legitimate job created removes one more potential recruit from the marketplace of violence. Fourth, we must distinguish legitimate grievances from criminality. Every democracy must preserve space for peaceful disagreement. Citizens have the right to express their concerns lawfully. But criminal violence must never be confused with political expression. At the same time, governments must ensure that peaceful voices always have legitimate avenues through which they can be heard. When dialogue disappears, extremism often fills the vacuum. Strong governments do not fear conversation. They encourage it. Fifth, regional collaboration is no longer optional. Criminal organisations do not recognise state boundaries. Our response cannot stop at state boundaries either. The South-East has an opportunity to demonstrate what coordinated regional security can achieve through intelligence sharing, harmonised emergency response, integrated technology, joint operational planning, and sustained engagement among governors, security agencies, traditional institutions, and community leaders. Competition among states must never become competition in security. Security is strongest when cooperation becomes institutional rather than occasional. Sixth, our national security architecture must continually evolve to strengthen both operational effectiveness and national cohesion. Permit me to make one critical observation. As military officers, we are trained to think not only about the deployment of forces, but also about the strategic message that force structure conveys. The recent expansion of Nigeria’s military formations is a welcome acknowledgement that our evolving security environment demands stronger institutional capacity. It recognises that yesterday’s force structure may no longer be adequate for today’s realities. However, every decision regarding the location of major military formations carries both operational and symbolic significance. The South-East occupies a critical position within our federation. It is strategically located, economically vibrant, commercially indispensable, and, both geographically and demographically, larger than some regions that currently host three divisional headquarters. Against this background, the absence of a comparable divisional formation within the South-East naturally invites reflection-not as a matter of regional rivalry or grievance, but as a question of strategic planning and national integration. Military divisions are more than administrative headquarters. They strengthen command and control. They improve operational responsiveness. They enhance intelligence coordination. They deepen civil-military cooperation. They stimulate economic activity. Above all, they reassure citizens that they are fully represented within the nation’s security architecture. In national security, perception often reinforces capability. When citizens believe that national institutions are fairly structured and equitably distributed, confidence grows. Confidence strengthens cooperation. And cooperation remains one of the most valuable force multipliers available to any security organisation. I fully appreciate that force disposition must always be guided by professional military judgement rather than politics. Nevertheless, strategic reviews should remain dynamic, with periodic assessments of whether force structures adequately reflect emerging threats, demographic realities, economic significance, and the overriding imperative of national cohesion. A secure Nigeria must also be a Nigeria in which every geopolitical zone sees itself as a full stakeholder in both the responsibilities and the institutions charged with protecting our collective future. Ladies and Gentlemen, permit me one final observation drawn from military experience: Battles are won by tactics. Wars are won by strategy. But peace is won by legitimacy. Our nation has invested significantly in security personnel, equipment, and operational capabilities. We must now invest with equal determination in strengthening public confidence, accountable institutions, inclusive governance, and equal opportunity. Citizens willingly defend societies they believe belong to them. That is perhaps the greatest strategic advantage any nation can possess. The South-East has always been known for enterprise. For education. For innovation. For resilience. For community organisation. These enduring strengths remain among our greatest security assets. Let us therefore reject fear. Let us reject division. Let us reject every attempt to define our future by insecurity. Instead, let us build a region where governments, security agencies, traditional institutions, religious bodies, civil society, the private sector, and ordinary citizens work together in genuine partnership. Because lasting peace is never imposed. It is earned. It is nurtured. It is built. One community. One institution. One generation at a time. One final observation concerns the way we conduct our politics. Too often, our politics is unnecessarily divisive and, in many instances, descends into violence. Democracy was never intended to be an end in itself. It is a means of advancing the common good and improving the lives of the people. When political actors resort to violence to settle disagreements, they undermine the very democratic system they claim to defend. More importantly, they weaken the moral distinction between political violence and the criminal violence that threatens our society. Leadership carries a higher obligation. Those entrusted with public responsibility must demonstrate that disagreement need not lead to hostility, and that political competition can coexist with respect for the rule of law, democratic institutions, and the sanctity of human life. If we cannot model these values, we should not expect others to embrace them. May today’s deliberations produce practical and lasting solutions that strengthen security, restore public confidence, and reinforce the unity and prosperity of both the South-East and the Federal Republic of Nigeria. Thank you. God bless the South-East. God bless the Federal Republic of Nigeria. I commend the Government and the organisers once again for convening this summit. May today’s deliberations produce practical, courageous, and enduring solutions that strengthen not only the South-East, but also the unity, security, and prosperity of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. Thank you. God bless the South-East. God bless the Federal Republic of Nigeria. Being an address by Sen. General Ike Omar Sanda Nwachukwu, GCMG, CFR, COM, psc+, mni, fniia, etc., at the South-East Regional Security Summit held in Umuahia on 30th July 2026 The post Measures to tackle security challenges in Southeast Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Espace numérique: une stratégie interministérielle pour protéger les enfants des risques en ligne
items.description: Le gouvernement a mis en place une initiative nationale baptisée «Culture numérique/Protection des enfants sur Internet» pilotée par l'Agence de développement du digital (ADD) pour renforcer la protection des enfants sur l'espace numérique, a indiqué la ministre déléguée chargée de la Transition numérique et de la réforme de l'administration, Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni. Dans une réponse à une question parlementaire écrite signée par le député Khalid Essatte, la ministre a assuré que l'exécutif avait mis en place une stratégie rassemblant plusieurs intervenants, dans un objectif de prévention et de sensibilisation auprès du jeune public. Elle a mis en avant la constitution d'une commission nationale de coordination incluant les ministères de la Transition numérique, de l'Éducation nationale, de la Jeunesse, de l'Intérieur, ainsi que la Direction générale de la sécurité des systèmes d'information (DGSSI), la Direction générale de la Sûreté nationale (DGSN), l'Agence nationale de réglementation des télécommunications (ANRT), et l'Observatoire national des droits de l'enfant. Tout en reconnaissant que les technologies numériques constituent un levier essentiel de développement économique et social, Amal El Fallah Seghrouchni, a mis en garde contre les effets d'une utilisation non maîtrisée, susceptible d'avoir des conséquences psychologiques, sociales et sanitaires sur les enfants. Elle insiste, à ce titre, sur la nécessité de promouvoir une culture du numérique responsable dès le plus jeune âge. Elle a mis en avant des partenariats avec les établissements d'enseignement, les associations ainsi que des ONG internationales pour travailler à développer un système éducatif sur des plateformes pédagogiques sécurisées, des formations et des programmes de sensibilisation destinés aux élèves et aux membres de l'éducation. La ministre a également évoque la plateforme himaya.gov.ma qui a été créé pour la protection des enfants sur l'espace numérique. Seghrouchni a indiqué que la plateforme compte déjà près de 45.000 utilisateurs et propose plusieurs services destinés aux enfants, aux parents ainsi qu'aux éducateurs. Et de rappeler que la plateforme himaya.gov.ma communique les bonnes pratiques d'utilisation d'Internet, œuvre à sensibiliser les différentes catégories concernées aux risques numériques, et à fournir des conseils pratiques aux familles. The post Espace numérique: une stratégie interministérielle pour protéger les enfants des risques en ligne appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Tinubu didn’t insult Catholic bishops; he’s one of their best friends — Orji Kalu
items.description: Senator representing Abia North, Orji Uzor Kalu, has defended President Bola Tinubu against allegations that he disrespected the Catholic Church, insisting that the President enjoys a cordial relationship with the Catholic bishops and has always maintained an open-door policy towards them. Kalu made the remarks on Wednesday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today while reacting to the controversy that followed the recent meeting between President Tinubu and members of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria (CBCN). The controversy was fuelled by comments from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) vice-presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, who alleged that Tinubu had insulted the Catholic bishops following the meeting. However, Kalu rejected the claim, maintaining that there was no disrespect towards the Church. “This is not the first time that the Catholic Church is going to President Tinubu. In every country, from DRC to Angola, to South Africa and anywhere, the Catholic Church and other churches are always the conscience of the country,” he said. The former Abia State governor noted that the concerns raised after the meeting reflected the longstanding tradition of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Nigeria, which he said has consistently commented on national issues since the era of military rule. “I do not see anything wrong in what the Catholic bishops said. Those discussions were made by Archbishop Danagoro of Kaduna State, the current president of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference, and not even Onaiyekan,” Kalu stated. He added, “Since the military rule, the Catholic Bishops’ Conference hold its conference every year where they talk and issue a statement about the state of the nation.” Kalu further stressed that Tinubu should not be viewed as an adversary of the Catholic Church. “For me, Tinubu is not an enemy to the Catholic bishops; he’s one of their best friends and I don’t feel insulted. Tinubu in no means insulted the Catholic bishops. I didn’t see it,” he said. Highlighting the relationship between the presidency and the Church, Kalu said Tinubu has consistently granted requests for meetings from Catholic leaders. “President Tinubu has a very good relationship with the Catholic Church. Anytime they have asked for an audience, he has given it to them because any president dodging Catholic bishops is dodging himself, because what politicians cannot tell the president, the Catholic bishops will say it,” he added. The post Tinubu didn’t insult Catholic bishops; he’s one of their best friends — Orji Kalu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NPP demands update on galamsey fight, helicopter crash probe ahead of first anniversary of tragedy
items.description: The opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) has called on the government to account for progress made in the fight against illegal mining and provide an update on investigations into the military helicopter crash that claimed the lives of eight people a year ago. The party made the call in a statement issued on Wednesday, August 5, ahead of the first anniversary of the August 6, 2025 tragedy. The NPP joined the government, the Ghana Armed Forces, bereaved families and Ghanaians in commemorating the victims, including Defence Minister Dr Edward Omane Boamah, Environment, Science and Technology Minister Alhaji Ibrahim Murtala Muhammed, Acting Deputy National Security Coordinator Alhaji Muniru Mohammed, Dr Samuel Sarpong, Mr Samuel Aboagye and three Ghana Armed Forces crew members. The party also encouraged public participation in the nationwide blood donation exercise organised in their honour. According to the statement signed by General Secretary Justin Kodua Frimpong, the eight died while on a national mission to Obuasi to combat illegal mining and protect Ghana’s lands and water bodies. It argued that the most meaningful way to honour their sacrifice was not only through memorial events but by demonstrating tangible progress in the anti-galamsey campaign. The NPP therefore urged the government to present evidence on the current state of the country’s rivers and water bodies, the extent of forest reserve restoration and the overall impact of efforts to curb illegal mining over the past year. It also called for a comprehensive update on the official investigation into the helicopter crash, including its findings, safety recommendations and measures implemented to prevent a recurrence. The party maintained that remembrance must be accompanied by accountability, pledging to continue demanding answers on both the anti-galamsey campaign and the circumstances surrounding the fatal mission. It concluded by praying for the souls of the eight victims to rest in peace and for Ghana to honour their sacrifice through responsible leadership and action.

items.title: Effiduase-Asokore MP calls for faithful servants of God to inspire hope in youth
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Effiduase-Asokore Constituency in the Ashanti Region, Dr. Ayew Afriyie, has underscored the need for Ghana to have genuine and faithful men of God who are committed to empowering and motivating the younger generation with hope, purpose, and direction through the Word of God. Dr. Afriyie expressed concern over what he described as a growing wave of hopelessness among young people, fueled by negative narratives in society. He made the remarks during the Kumasi edition of “Invasion 2026” organized by Prophet Benjamin Fordjour Ministries at the PENSA Auditorium, Ayeduase, in the Oforikrom Municipality. The lawmaker revealed that some individuals have deliberately polluted the minds of the youth with the notion that there is no future for them in Ghana, a development he believes must be countered with sound biblical teaching and mentorship. Held under the theme ‘FAITH’ and anchored on Hebrews 11:1, “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen”, the event attracted hundreds of believers from Kumasi and surrounding communities, as youth constituted approximately 80% of the congregation. It was a night when faith was stirred, lives were transformed, and destinies were awakened. Attendees experienced hours of intense worship, prophetic ministrations, and teachings centered on building faith in God amid current economic and social challenges. Addressing the gathering, Dr. Afriyie, who is also the Ranking Member of the Parliamentary Select Committee on Health, said the youth can only thrive if they are grounded in faith and equipped with inspiration to pursue their dreams. “If we fill our young people with the Word and with hope, they will not give up. They will wake up, prepare themselves, and position themselves for a better future,” he stated. He added that men of God have a critical responsibility to serve as agents of transformation by speaking life into the youth and guiding them away from despair, drug abuse, and social vices. Dr. Afriyie commended Prophet Benjamin Fordjour and his ministry for their consistency in organizing programs that promote spiritual renewal and national transformation. “I want to commend Prophet Benjamin Fordjour Ministries for this wonderful initiative. Programs like ‘Invasion’ remind our young people that God has not forgotten them and that their best days are ahead,” he said. He further urged religious leaders, parents, and policymakers to collaborate in mentoring the youth, noting that a generation rooted in faith and discipline is key to Ghana’s development. Prophet Benjamin Fordjour, host of the “Invasion” and Founder of Prophet Benjamin Fordjour Ministries, said the program was birthed out of a burden to see total transformation in the lives of people, particularly the younger generation. According to him, “Invasion” was designed as more than a church program. It is a spiritual movement intended to ignite faith, restore hope, and reposition believers for impact in their families, schools, workplaces, and communities. “The goal is simple: to bring people back to God. When God becomes the center of your life, no matter the economic hardship, no matter the social pressure, you will stand. That is the kind of transformation we are praying for,” he said. Prophet Fordjour charged the youth to prioritize their relationship with God above trends and distractions. He urged them to make God the center of every decision and circumstance, stressing that divine direction is key to succeeding in life. He also admonished them to stay away from indecent behavior, substance abuse, and other vices that he said were derailing the potential of many young people across the country. Reflecting on the journey of “Invasion,” Prophet Fordjour noted that since its inception 16 years ago, the program has grown into a dynamic annual gathering known for intense worship, prophecy, deliverance, and teachings that inspire spiritual renewal. “This is not just an event. For 16 years, God has used ‘Invasion’ to touch lives, heal the brokenhearted, and raise a generation that will serve Him with passion,” he added. The highly anticipated revival gathering concluded with prayer sessions for the nation, the youth, and leaders, as many attendees testified to receiving direction and encouragement for their personal lives and careers. The Kingdom Revival Gathering of miracles, healing, worship, and prophetic encounters featured powerful ministrations from renowned ministers of God, including Efe Grace, Jojo Arhin, and Quame Gyedu, with Pastor Badu Kyenkyenhene as Guest.

items.title: Lagos–Calabar coastal highway already beyond Lagos, Presidency replies Duke
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru The Presidency on Wednesday dismissed criticism from the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) presidential candidate, Mr. Donald Duke, that the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway would not extend beyond Epe in Lagos State, saying the project has already reached Ogun State. The Presidency said the former Cross River State governor’s criticism was politically motivated and not rooted in fact. Donald Duke was governor of Cross River State from 1999 to 2007 and was also the Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate in 2019. Reacting to the comment attributed to Duke — that the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway would not go beyond Lagos — the Presidency said the PRP candidate’s remarks were in poor taste.’ Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Publicity, Tope Ajayi, said Duke was “arguing against reality” by claiming the highway would not extend beyond Lagos and by questioning the project’s priority. In a post on his verified X account, the presidential aide said: “Former Governor Donald Duke, who wants to become President on the banner of an unviable political platform, has also joined the chorus of those saying the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway will not go beyond Lagos State. “I think politics makes a lot of people say things they don’t mean or believe. They just talk for the sake of talking or because of bad politics. There is actually no sense in arguing against reality. “While Duke was saying on TV that the Coastal Highway won’t go beyond Epe, the project has reached Ogun State, and work is ongoing on the Ondo and Akwa Ibom State sections of the coastal road.” The post Lagos–Calabar coastal highway already beyond Lagos, Presidency replies Duke appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Jets de déchets sur les voies de la ligne TGM | La Transtu portera plainte
items.description: La Société des transports de Tunis (Transtu) a fait part de son indignation suite à un acte d'incivilité flagrant survenu au niveau de la station Le Kram, sur la ligne de la banlieue nord Tunis-Goulette-Marsa (TGM). Des riverains et des commerçants avoisinants ont délibérément jeté leurs ordures ménagères et divers déchets directement sur les voies ferrées. En plus des nuisances environnementales et de la dégradation esthétique du site, ces pratiques irresponsables représentent un danger réel pour la sécurité de la circulation des rames. Dans un communiqué, la Transtu a exprimé son profond regret et sa vive condamnation face à la récurrence de ces comportements, tout en rappelant que ces actes ne se contentent pas de perturber le service public et de mettre en péril la sécurité des usagers, mais qu'ils constituent également des infractions pénales punies par la loi. Tout en renouvelant son appel aux habitants et aux commerçants à respecter les règles élémentaires de propreté, la Transtu confirme qu'elle engagera des poursuites judiciaires, en coordination avec les autorités sécuritaires et locales, contre toute personne impliquée dans la détérioration des infrastructures publiques ou la mise en danger du trafic ferroviaire. items.title: Nigeria : plus de 300 victimes d’enlèvements libérées (gouvernement)
items.description: Le gouvernement nigérian a annoncé mercredi la libération de 308 victimes d'enlèvements, dont 163 enlevées plus tôt cette année dans un seul village. « Le président Bola Ahmed Tinubu se félicite chaleureusement du sauvetage réussi de 308 citoyens nigérians qui avaient été enlevés lors de différentes attaques dans les États du Niger et de Kwara », a déclaré le porte-parole présidentiel Bayo Onanuga. Les enlèvements contre rançon perpétrés par des groupes criminels, des jihadistes et des gangs connus sous le nom de bandits sont récurrents au Nigeria, en particulier dans les zones du nord et du centre du pays où la présence de l'État est limitée. En février, des jihadistes sont présumés avoir attaqué le village de Woro, dans l'État de Kwara, près de la frontière avec le Bénin, tuant plus de 150 personnes et en enlevant un nombre resté indéterminé. « Le président Bola Ahmed Tinubu se félicite chaleureusement du sauvetage réussi de 308 citoyens nigérians qui avaient été enlevés lors de différentes attaques dans les États du Niger et de Kwara », a déclaré le porte-parole présidentiel Bayo Onanuga. Il a précisé que 163 provenaient de Woro « et 145 de l'État du Niger ». Les victimes ont été libérées d'un lieu situé dans la forêt du parc national du lac Kainji. Les vastes forêts et réserves du pays, souvent mal contrôlées, sont transformées en repaires pour les groupes criminels nigérians. Il s'agissait de « la plus grande opération de sauvetage jamais réalisée en une seule journée », a affirmé M. Onanuga. Des jihadistes sont présumés avoir semé la terreur à Woro après avoir envoyé une lettre au village pour annoncer leur intention de prêcher, sans que personne ne se présente. Ils ont incendié des maisons, tué plus de 165 personnes et enlevé un nombre indéterminé d'habitants, ont déclaré des résidents à l'AFP à l'époque, même si les autorités locales ont communiqué un bilan inférieur. Selon les médias, le nombre de personnes enlevées s'élevait à 176, bien que, pas plus tard que vendredi, la police de l'État de Kwara ait indiqué que ce chiffre n'était pas étayé. Une partie du village avait été réduite en cendres lors de l'attaque. Le président Tinubu a condamné cette « attaque bestiale », déployant un bataillon de l'armée dans la région et en imputant la responsabilité au mouvement islamiste Boko Haram, bien que ce nom soit souvent utilisé de manière générique pour désigner les groupes jihadistes au Nigeria. Quelques mois plus tôt, le Groupe de soutien à l'islam et aux musulmans (JNIM), lié à Al-Qaïda, avait revendiqué sa première attaque sur le sol nigérian dans l'État de Kwara, près de Woro. AFP

Abuja experiences earth tremor again, as Alake calms residents
items.description: By Gabriel Ewepu Thw Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Tuesday, again experienced a 1-kilometre depth of earth tremor shaking several buildings and spread across a distance of four kilometres in five seconds. This was contained in a statement signed on Wednesday by the Special Assistant on Media to the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Lara Owoeye-Wise. Owoeye-Wise said the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, calmed Abuja residents over the earth tremor as he “has directed the Nigerian Geological Survey Agency (NGSA) to provide hourly updates of the seismic developments around Abuja, the Federal Capital to him for regular review and possible escalation to other relevant agencies. “Urging residents of the Federal Capital to go about their normal routine without anxiety, Alake, who is currently engaging American investors on joint venture proposals in the solid minerals sector in Washington DC, United States said other proactive measures have been deployed to ensure the safety of residents and properties. “He was responding to an alert by the NGSA, reporting that tremors shook several buildings in Abuja on Tuesday, August 4, this year.” According to her, “The NGSA Seismic Monitoring Station, Utako, recorded the earth tremor at exactly 11.23.27am, noting that it originated from a 1-kilometre depth and spread across a distance of four kilometres in five seconds. However, the NGSA interpreted the tremor as a ” light event of I to II magnitude on the Mercalli scale.” “Its words: ” This is a characteristic feature of a surface earth tremor that poses no threat to lives and properties except for the discomfort of the shake and fear of possible destruction.” She also said, “The Minister assured the public that the agency will continue to monitor the situation while residents engage in normal activities.” The post Abuja experiences earth tremor again, as Alake calms residents appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le ministre Abdourahmane Diouf porte la voix du Président Diomaye Faye au Forum Infra for Africa 2026 à Dar es Salaam
items.description: Le ministre de l'Énergie et du Pétrole, El Hadji Abdourahmane Diouf, a représenté le Président de la République Bassirou Diomaye Faye au Forum Infra for Africa 2026, tenu à Dar es Salaam sous le haut patronage de la Présidente tanzanienne, Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan. Organisée par Africa50, cette rencontre a rassemblé les principaux décideurs du continent autour du financement des infrastructures et de la transition énergétique. Dans un communiqué publié à l'issue de sa mission, le ministre a indiqué avoir accompli cette tâche « avec un profond sens de l'honneur ». Un plaidoyer pour une transition énergétique « juste, souveraine et inclusive » Point d'orgue de son déplacement, El Hadji Abdourahmane Diouf a pris part à un panel ministériel réunissant plusieurs de ses homologues africains ainsi que le Secrétaire général de la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (ZLECAf). Il y a défendu la position sénégalaise en matière énergétique, plaidant pour « une transition énergétique juste, souveraine et inclusive, fondée sur la valorisation responsable de nos ressources gazières au service de notre industrialisation et du développement durable du continent africain ». Un tête-à-tête stratégique avec la BAD En marge du forum, le ministre a également été reçu par le Président du Groupe de la Banque africaine de développement (BAD), Dr Sidi Ould Tah. Selon le communiqué, ces échanges ont porté sur « le renforcement du partenariat stratégique entre le Sénégal et la BAD », avec un accent particulier sur trois chantiers : le Partenariat pour une transition énergétique juste (JETP), l'initiative Mission 300, ainsi que des investissements visant à « accélérer l'accès de nos populations à une énergie fiable, abordable et durable ». Au terme de sa mission, le ministre a résumé la portée de sa participation en des termes qui se veulent à la fois bilatéraux et panafricains : cette visite aura été, selon ses mots, l'occasion de « réaffirmer l'engagement du Sénégal en faveur d'une Afrique plus intégrée, plus résiliente et plus prospère ». O.B.N C’est avec un profond sens de l’honneur que j’ai représenté Son Excellence Monsieur le Président de la République au Forum Infra for Africa 2026, à Dar es Salaam sous le haut patronage de Son Excellence Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan, Présidente de la République Unie de Tanzanie. Cette… pic.twitter.com/SwzVRDF0EO — Dr El Hadji Abdourahmane DIOUF (@drelhadjiAdiouf) August 5, 2026

items.title: NAICOM revokes Nigeria Reinsurance’s licence, appoints Muiz Banire as receiver/liquidator
items.description: By Innocent Anaba The National Insurance Commission, NAICOM, has revoked the operating licence of Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation over its failure to meet the statutory Minimum Capital Requirement, MCR, and appointed Dr. Muiz Banire, SAN, as Receiver/Provisional Liquidator to wind up the company’s affairs. The appointment took effect on August 3, 2026, following the cancellation of the corporation’s certificate of registration by the insurance regulator. In a public notice dated August 4, 2026, Banire said he was appointed by NAICOM, in exercise of its statutory powers, to take charge of the receivership and liquidation of Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation (RR-002). According to the notice, the company’s licence was revoked after it failed to comply with the prescribed Minimum Capital Requirement applicable to its category of licence within the stipulated compliance period, in accordance with the Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act (NIIRA) 2025 and other extant laws, regulations and guidelines. Banire said his appointment empowers him to immediately trace, recover, secure and take possession of all assets belonging to the company, collate and settle its liabilities in accordance with the NIIRA 2025, liaise with NAICOM on matters relating to the liquidation, and submit periodic reports to the Commission. He also directed banks, financial institutions, insurance policyholders and members of the public not to honour any instruction relating to the company except those issued by him or persons expressly authorised by him. As part of the liquidation process, Banire announced that all bank accounts belonging to Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation had been frozen with immediate effect pending further directives from his office. He warned that any transaction carried out without his authorisation would be at the risk of the parties involved. “Members of the general public, banks and financial institutions in Nigeria are hereby informed that no financial transactions should be conducted pursuant to any instruction from anyone except those that I issue as the Receiver/Provisional Liquidator,” the notice stated. According to him, only instructions bearing his official seal and stamp as a legal practitioner, or those issued by persons duly authorised by him, will be recognised throughout the liquidation process. The regulatory action marks a significant enforcement measure by NAICOM and underscores the Commission’s resolve to ensure that insurance and reinsurance companies operating in Nigeria comply with statutory capital requirements designed to safeguard policyholders and strengthen the financial stability of the industry. The liquidation process is expected to involve the recovery and realisation of the company’s assets, verification and settlement of valid claims and liabilities, and the orderly winding up of its affairs in accordance with the provisions of the law. The public notice serves as formal notification to policyholders, creditors, banks and other stakeholders that all dealings concerning Nigeria Reinsurance Corporation must henceforth, be channelled through the Receiver/Provisional Liquidator until the liquidation process is concluded. The post NAICOM revokes Nigeria Reinsurance’s licence, appoints Muiz Banire as receiver/liquidator appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lille cible un jeune talent du Real Madrid pour remplacer Ayyoub Bouaddi
items.description: Alors qu'Ayyoub Bouaddi se rapproche d'un transfert vers Manchester City, le LOSC aurait déjà identifié le profil appelé à lui succéder. Selon le quotidien espagnol Marca, le club nordiste s'intéresse au jeune milieu de terrain du Real Madrid, Jorge Cestero. Le mercato estival s'annonce particulièrement animé du côté de Lille. Avec l'arrivée de Davide Ancelotti sur le banc et les départs de plusieurs cadres, dont Chancel Mbemba, Aïssa Mandi et Thomas Meunier, la direction lilloise travaille activement à remodeler son effectif en vue de la prochaine saison, marquée notamment par une participation à la Ligue des champions. Parmi les dossiers prioritaires figure celui d'Ayyoub Bouaddi. Le milieu de terrain marocain de 18 ans est annoncé avec insistance du côté de Manchester City, où les négociations seraient désormais bien avancées. Auteur d'une Coupe du monde 2026 remarquée avec les Lions de l'Atlas, Bouaddi est considéré comme l'un des plus grands espoirs européens à son poste. Lille espérerait récupérer plus de 100 millions d'euros dans cette opération. Afin d'anticiper son départ, les dirigeants nordistes auraient pris contact avec le Real Madrid pour s'informer de la situation de Jorge Cestero. Âgé de 20 ans, le milieu défensif évolue avec le Real Madrid Castilla et fait partie des joueurs les plus prometteurs du centre de formation madrilène. Ancien entraîneur de la réserve merengue, Álvaro Arbeloa n'avait d'ailleurs pas hésité à qualifier Cestero de « meilleur milieu défensif d'Espagne » , mettant en avant sa lecture du jeu, sa qualité technique et sa capacité à organiser le jeu depuis l'entrejeu. Arrivé au Real Madrid en 2019, le natif de Saragosse a progressivement gravi les échelons grâce à ses performances régulières. Solide à la récupération, il se distingue également par sa faculté à casser les lignes adverses et à résister au pressing, des qualités qui correspondent au profil recherché par Lille pour remplacer Bouaddi. Sous contrat avec le Real Madrid jusqu'en 2028, Jorge Cestero est suivi de près par le club madrilène, qui envisage à moyen terme son intégration dans l'équipe première. Le jeune Espagnol a déjà participé à plusieurs séances d'entraînement avec les professionnels et a effectué ses débuts avec l'équipe première face à Benfica en Ligue des champions. Si un transfert définitif reste une possibilité, l'hypothèse d'un prêt est également étudiée. Une formule qui permettrait au Real Madrid d'offrir du temps de jeu à l'un de ses plus grands espoirs, tandis que Lille miserait une nouvelle fois sur un jeune talent à fort potentiel pour assurer la succession d'Ayyoub Bouaddi. The post Lille cible un jeune talent du Real Madrid pour remplacer Ayyoub Bouaddi appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Fraud could erode Ghana’s financial inclusion gains if trust is lost – Digital Finance Practitioner warns
items.description: Fraud poses one of the greatest threats to Ghana’s efforts to deepen financial inclusion and could reverse years of progress if it is not addressed effectively, William Nana Danso Abeam, Country Head of Consumer and Commercial Banking Products at Ecobank Group Plc, has cautioned. Speaking on Joy Business Masterclass hosted by Yaw Anim Barnafo, Mr. Abeam said trust remains the foundation of digital financial services and is critical to expanding access to banking and other financial products. The discussion formed part of a month-long discussion on Understanding Financial Inclusion , where he explored the growing role of fraud as a major barrier to financial inclusion in the digital age. According to him, the increasing sophistication of fraudsters and the growing number of attacks across the financial services industry are threatening public confidence in digital financial platforms, making trust management a strategic priority. “If you ask me to select or maybe make a choice of one big risk or one thing that would stand in our way with the progress that we are making with financial inclusion, because we are now leveraging more on digital, it is the issue of trust. People would need to trust the system; trust is key, and I think that if we don’t deal with the issue of fraud very well, it will erode the trust that we have in the platforms that are enabling financial inclusion. And it’s not one person’s job when it comes to fraud. Everybody is included. Everybody plays a role. From you, the consumer, to the banks, to the fintechs, to the mobile money network operators, to the telcos, to the government. Everybody has a role to play,” he said. Mr. Abeam stressed that fraud has evolved into a much broader challenge than many people initially assumed. He explained that while early incidents were largely associated with mobile money services, fraudsters have expanded their operations to target banks, investment companies, and insurance firms, making the issue one that affects the entire financial ecosystem. “Because, you see, when fraud in the space started, people thought it was just the mobile money issue. But not long after they moved from the mobile money stage, they hit the banks; now they are hitting investment companies and insurance companies, so it’s everybody in the space, all the services we provide,” he added. He also warned that fraudsters have become significantly more sophisticated, making it increasingly difficult for individuals to identify fraudulent attempts, saying, “What is scary about it is that, years ago, you know, when people start talking, you know this person is not very educated, so by the grammar, you can easily identify them, but these days very sophisticated people are going in there, so we all need to come together and support the drive against fraud.” Mr. Abeam noted that social engineering remains one of the most commonly used tactics employed by fraudsters to gain access to victims’ personal information and financial accounts. “You, the customer, must be involved, get to know, I mean, people will call you, and you know, the user social engineering is the most utilized form; you know, they call you, they pick information, and they use that to actually have access,” he emphasised. He therefore called for greater collaboration among consumers, banks, fintech companies, mobile money operators, telecommunications companies, and government institutions to strengthen the country’s fight against financial crime. According to him, preserving public confidence in digital financial platforms is essential to ensuring more people continue to adopt formal banking services and digital financial solutions. “We need everybody to be involved when it comes to fraud. Else, the progress we are making will be eroded because people would lose trust in the system,” he stated. Mr. Abeam concluded that protecting trust is no longer only a banking concern but a shared national responsibility, warning that failure to tackle fraud effectively could undermine Ghana’s financial inclusion agenda and slow the country’s transition towards a more digitally connected financial system. Joy Business Masterclass airs every Wednesday at 1:15 p.m. on Joy FM and is hosted by Yaw Anim Barnafo.

items.title: A Biopic That Ends Right When It’s Getting Started
items.description: Tony follows a very familiar sort of 19-year-old menace—the kind of character coming-of-age movies like this were made for. He’s someone you might have crushed on in college: He sulks around with worldly paperbacks stuffed into his rear pockets, dresses in leather jackets even if it’s unseasonably warm, and seems to wear a permanent glower. Yet Tony, as played by Dominic Sessa, is more than just a pretentious bad boy; he’s starting to work his way toward something meaningful. His full name also just so happens to be Anthony Bourdain , who the audience likely knows will one day become a renowned chef and author, tapping his back-of-house experiences for material; eventually, his celebrity as a TV personality will transcend his punchy writing about the life of a cook. The film, directed and co-written by Matt Johnson, should be hamstrung by this conclusion. On paper, Tony sounds like it requires the audience to understand something that doesn’t happen during the movie; it saves calling Tony by his full name until its final moments. This often irritating, barely grown dilettante will become someone important when he does a little more maturing, off-screen. The truth about Bourdain, however, is that he really was a cinematic figure , even in his wayward adolescence—at least if his evocative writing on that period is to be believed. Tony draws from Kitchen Confidential , Bourdain’s 2000 best seller that laid bare the rough-and-tumble world of haute cuisine from the perspective of a jaded yet passionate New York chef. But the screenplay adapts only the early chapters, which cover Bourdain’s tentative beginnings in the cooking profession, including one teenage summer he spent, frequently hungover, working in the kitchen of a seafood restaurant on Cape Cod. Presenting that appetizer as a rich, earthy main course somehow comes together beautifully. Tony is not burdened by the complex details of Bourdain’s adult life, and Sessa is not asked to imitate a well-known man who spent the latter half of his career on TV. Instead, he just has to capture the feeling of possibility, wrapped up in the recognizable foolishness of youth. He and Johnson both do a beautiful job of it. [ Read: The missing pieces of Anthony Bourdain ] The viewer meets Tony at Vassar College, where he spent two years before dropping out. The school year is over, and he’s hoping to gain a summer writing fellowship that will impress his ditzy dad, Pierre (played by Rich Sommer), and his far more judgmental mother, Gladys (Dagmara Domińczyk). When that falls through, Tony instead follows a crush named Nancy (Emilia Jones) to Provincetown, Massachusetts, where she has a summer job; he eventually stumbles into a gig washing dishes at the Flagship, a seafood spot. The staff is made up of the hard-partying guys one might expect (including a garrulous Stavros Halkias and a brooding Leo Woodall). For much of the run time, Tony is an observer, sucking up what knowledge he can while trying to project a precious aloofness—a trait that beguiles many a young man in search of inspiration. His muse is found, primarily, in a character simply called “Chef” (Antonio Banderas). He’s a wise, older Brazilian man who silently greets the ocean every morning and still loves his trade enough to make his own ketchup rather than buy bottles of Heinz. Banderas could play this role in his sleep: the meditative, somewhat elusive mentor, delivering advice with simultaneous bluntness and poeticism. But he might actually be the best actor alive who could inhabit that sort of sensei role without it feeling clichéd and off-the-rack. Chef exists mostly to invest Tony with a sense of pride in what he does, even if it’s the manual labor of cooking rather than whatever intellectual pursuits Tony thinks he should follow. Johnson understands that this respect for artistry was what made Bourdain such an enduring figure. That inherent empathy is how Tony gets away with being a biopic that ends in the early chapters of a person’s life. It’s an origin story for how a man became a chef, yes, yet it’s more concerned with how someone might fall in love with a scrappy culture and the beautiful way that cuisine blends the highbrow and the low. Tony is learning how to create shellfish delicacies; at the same time, he’s cracking open oysters and cleaning plates. (He’s also holding his own among seedy, profane company, the kind of ribald back-and-forth that Johnson can present with hilarious immediacy—be it in his prior biopic, BlackBerry , or in the riotous Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie .) Although Tony is a necessarily minor piece of storytelling, it feels deceptively major nevertheless—and is infused with just enough of its subject’s real-world charisma.
